chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ali ibn Ribat, from Ibn Muskhan, from Layth al-Muradi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the fasting person who undergoes cupping and pours oil into his ear. He said, 'There is no harm, except for snuff (sua'at), for it is disliked.'
ai.seo_question: Does cupping or putting oil in the ear break the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that cupping and ear oil do not invalidate the fast, distinguishing between external application and ingestion. Notably, while snuff (sua'at) is deemed *makruh* (disliked) rather than strictly invalidating, it is singled out due to the potential for particles to reach the throat, reflecting the Shia juristic focus on the precise mechanism of breaking the fast. This highlights the nuanced approach of the Imams in differentiating between actions that nullify the fast and those that merely diminish its spiritual perfection.
